featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dumpling Khang is a place I’ve been going to since 2019 — I still remember the first time I tried their chicken thupka and how much I absolutely loved it. It had this authentic, comforting flavour that made me come back again and again. For a long time, I used to order their momo-thupka combo on a monthly basis — and back then it felt totally worth it. It was around ₹170, came with a generous bowl of soup and 6 momos, and tasted super fresh.

Over time, of course, the price went up (₹190… ₹200… and now it’s ₹320-350 if you order online), but what’s more disappointing is that the quality has definitely gone down. The thupka still hits on some days, but the momos have become really average — they taste like pre-packed ones just deep-fried and served. Not the fresh, soft, flavourful momos they used to be.

There’s also this dish called Laughing — which they hype up quite a bit — but honestly, it was very underwhelming. It’s basically some kind of roll (reminded me of Gujarati khaman) with Maggi/Wai Wai noodles stuffed inside, and that’s it. For the price, it really doesn’t deliver.

We also tried their Nepali thali on our recent visit — again, something they highly recommended. But that was another miss. It had rice, basic dal, some greens, one sabzi (usually an aloo sabzi), a small portion of chicken gravy and achar. It was okay, not bad, but definitely not something I’d go back for.

Now coming to the space itself — it’s tiny. Like, four tables tiny. So only four groups (of 3–4 people max) can sit at a time. Because of that, if you go during peak hours, it gets super crowded and you may have to wait. And even after placing your order, the food can take a while to arrive. That said, the place does give off a very warm, comforting, homely vibe. It’s the kind of small place that makes you want to curl up with soup on a rainy day.

They also usually do these combo offers during New Year and other festivals — where you get a set number of dishes or momos for a fixed price. I’d honestly recommend that more than dining in right now. The combos are way more reasonable and they get delivered to your home, so you skip the waiting and the crowd.

So yeah — if you’ve never tried it, go for their soups. They still remind me of the flavours from Himachal. But otherwise, the rest of the food is average, prices are high now, and the overall experience just isn’t what it used to be.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dynasty: The Indo-Chinese Restaurant That Doesn’t Need Buzz
Five stars aren’t enough, but they’ll have to do.
Dynasty operates in that rare territory where quality speaks louder than Instagram followers. This unpretentious neighborhood spot has mastered the art of authentic Indo-Chinese cooking — the kind that requires skill, not shortcuts.
Order the Chicken Lollipop and you’ll understand immediately. Each piece is a study in balance: crisp exterior, succulent interior, perfectly seasoned. The Manchow Soup arrives with the kind of umami depth that makes you wonder why other restaurants even bother. The Crispy Spinach Chicken demands respect, while the Crispy Thread Chicken delivers texture with purpose. These aren’t interpretations — they’re the genuine article.
But the real revelation lies in the Sour Chili and Sichuan dips. Layered, bold, and unapologetically complex, they’re the kind of accompaniments that transform a meal into an experience. The lemon iced tea cuts through it all with perfect timing.
What distinguishes Dynasty, though, is the service. The team moves with purpose, never intrusive, always present. It’s a family restaurant in the truest sense — one that makes you feel like you belong.
In a city saturated with forgettable Indo-Chinese, Dynasty reminds you why authenticity never goes out of style.

Dynasty Restaurant, Khar West: A Chinese Culinary Journey

Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West, Mumbai, is a haven for Chinese food enthusiasts. This popular eatery has been delighting taste buds with its authentic and flavorful dishes for years. Whether you're craving spicy, tangy, or sweet, Dynasty has something to offer.

One of the must-try dishes at Dynasty is their Crispy Spinach Paneer. This vegetarian delight features tender cubes of paneer coated in a crispy batter and tossed with fresh spinach. The combination of textures and flavors is simply irresistible. For a refreshing drink to complement your meal, try their Ice Lemon Tea. The tartness of the lemon combined with the sweetness of the tea makes it a perfect thirst quencher.

If you're looking for something spicy, the Paneer Chilli is a great option. Tender pieces of paneer are stir-fried with a spicy chili sauce, making it a fiery dish that will leave your taste buds tingling. For a unique twist on Chinese cuisine, try the Schezwan Crispy Veg. This dish features mixed vegetables coated in a crispy batter and tossed in a spicy Schezwan sauce.

For a satisfying main course, consider the Veg Burnt Garlic Rice or the Veg Malaysian Noodles. Both dishes are packed with flavor and are sure to leave you feeling full and satisfied. Dynasty also offers a variety of Indian Chinese dishes, combining traditional Indian flavors with Chinese cooking techniques.

To start your meal, the Manchow Soup is a classic choice. This flavorful soup is packed with vegetables and a hint of spice. For a refreshing and tangy drink, try the Sweet and Salty Lime Soda. The combination of sweet and salty flavors is a unique and refreshing treat.

Whether you're a seasoned Chinese food lover or new to the cuisine, Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West is a must-visit. With its delicious food, friendly service, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this restaurant is so popular among locals and tourists alike.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Today, during my visit to Mumbai, I had the pleasure of dining once again at Dakshin Garden Bar & Kitchen. This was my second time here, and once again, the experience was outstanding. I ordered the pomfret fish, tiger prawns, and mushroom tikka. Each dish was bursting with authentic flavors, and I especially appreciated that the kitchen adjusted the spice level to my preference—it made the food even more delicious and perfectly suited to my taste. The spices were bold and aromatic, truly showcasing the richness of Indian cuisine.

The atmosphere was warm and relaxing, while the staff were attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was just right. Every dish was cooked to perfection and full of flavor. Without a doubt, I will be returning on my next trip to Mumbai to enjoy this wonderful dining experience again.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik Gadgil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visit 1

I visited the place today. Mocktails & appetizers were amazing. The vegetable dumplings were unique. Mr Yogesh, the manager, offered me personalised services; the other servers were equally helpful and absolutely friendly. The main Course was average - I tasted some French Beans and Chicken. In the deserts, the Wasabi Cheese Case was fantastic.

Visit 3 [ Extract ]

Some of the dishes I had:

Duck [ in the main course, whose precise name I don't remember ] - Unusually strong on species, very much unauthentic, some pieces covered almost entirely in bones, and tough to chew upon. Call it a botched preparation and mood spoiler! It's not very often that I leave behind any dish. The grievance was resolved amicably.

Pork baos - You don't get these in many same-level restaurants, so a must-try. On a sweeter side and minced well and soft to consume. Arrived in the estimated time.

The quantity for all the dishes was above average and probably the largest I have seen at same-level restaurants.

Visit 4

A supreme and unforgettable experience

Some of the dishes I tried:

Traditional Pecking Duck - A conventional Chinese dish which is usually served with pancakes, troika of sauces, some veggies, and ofcourse, the duck cuts. Kudos to the chef, on my request, for serving me ready-made and saving me all the effort. The dish was slightly on the sweeter side, and the rolls had a good proportion of duck. Much laborious to scoff if all constituents are served separately.

Steamed Chilean Sea Bass - Prepared in soya ginger sauce, lightly spicy, mildly  pungent, and medium in size. Delicious, healthy and a must try. Maybe a few veggies at the side should be considered.

Light Breeze mocktail - Indeed light, mild soda, simple as it gets. Kinda like virgin mojito less Sprite/7UP and less coriander.

Grapefruit-based mocktail - the best of the three, authentic grapefruit flavour with medium bitterness, preserving the original taste, no soda.

Watermelon-based mocktail - another light one with no soda, pure watermelon [ and no syrup ] and a dash of cucumber.

I would like to thank Mr Jojo for preparing tailor-made off-the-menu [ above-mentioned ] mocktails, all of which were served inside 10 mins. And not to forget, offering me cashews which were off-the-menu. At the end, he also made an exception and served me the desserts from another restaurant because I didn't want any from the menu courtesy to various reasons.

This is amongst the handful of restaurants in this range where almost all the dishes are available in small and large sizes, and this allows one to make better selections on quantity. To add to that, even small sizes are equivalent to medium in many dishes. If I were to offer a suggestion, it would be to rejig the currently-mediocre dessert menu and add dishes like creme brulee, coconut pudding and cheese cake. On the embellishments front, I would say the restaurant is slightly behind despite the fact that they have a Chinese dragon hanging from the top & and a plush red carpet albeit the latter doesn't cover the flooring of the whole restaurant . The pots don't look very attractive and there is room for vibrance - a few paintings & art pieces could help. The restaurant size is quite big with 10+ tables.

It was also nice to meet & have an interlocution with Mr Srinivas, and I would like to thank him for personally overseeing the dinner and ensuring that it was a memorable experience. It is recherche of someone of his level to come down and discuss the ways certain past flaws were handled and briefing on the feedback taken to minimise the bitter moments; I really appreciate this commitment.

I am looking forward to visiting here again soon.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of bold flavors and comforting desi Chinese, Fat Kong is the kind of place that satisfies every craving with just the right hit of spice, crunch, and umami.

Crispy Chicken:
This dish was a knockout. The chicken pieces were perfectly battered—thin, golden, and fried to a shatteringly crisp texture. The outside had that addictive crunch, while the inside stayed juicy and tender. Tossed in a sticky, mildly spicy glaze with hints of garlic, soy, and chili, it was garnished with spring onions and sesame seeds, making it hard to stop at just one piece.

Chicken Triple Rice & Schezwan Noodles:
The Chicken Triple Rice was a full-on flavor bomb—a mix of fried rice and schezwan gravy poured generously on top, loaded with chopped veggies, chicken chunks, and a fried egg to top it all off. It was hearty, spicy, and soul-satisfying in that uniquely desi-Chinese way.

The Schezwan Noodles had a perfect wok-char (you know that smoky “wok hei” touch), with the right chewiness and a punchy garlic-chili flavor that didn’t overpower. Again, the chicken pieces were soft and well-seasoned, blending nicely with the heat of the schezwan sauce and the crunch of stir-fried vegetables.

Before the restaurant was located on SV Road Opposite Dynasty restaurant and everything was top class. It was one of those restaurants where we visited every weekend and it was always full so we had to wait 15 to 20 mins to get a table, and it was worth the wait.

So after around a decade I decided to revisit this restaurant for nostalgia and to try their iconic starters which made me drool earlier on.

So they are having two outlets now Jogeshwari and Khar, I visited the Khar outlet and was happy to see the restaurant maintaining their yellow and red colour theme. I was the only one present in their restaurant and was greeted by Akshay the person managing this outlet.

After requesting that I wish to try 2 dishes he was kind enough to give me 1/2 portion of my favourite Chicken Lollipop Hakka Style and Full portion of Crispy Spinach Chicken.

As soon as the lollipops were served the aroma transported me to the old era it was so beautiful and they have done well to maintain their taste as it was before.

But now comes the sad part, I got a piece of plastic spoon in my mouth while having the dish and was angry, disappointed and sad. I was advised by some of my friends that I should avoid the restaurant as it's not maintained the same way like before, but still I decided to try and I was like this is the end of Fatkongs for me.

I requested the Manager to not charge me for this dish and speak to the owner regarding this but he was helpless and they decided not to take away the charges.

Even though this incident took place I still ate the second dish Crispy Spinach Chicken, but it was nowhere close to the one which I used to eat before. The spinach didn't seem fresh and the chicken had a thick coating and wasn't good. So with a heavy heart I left the restaurant putting down a message to the owner who did give me a call and tried to give explanation and reasoning, though admitting that it wasn't right. But somehow I didn't feel like trying this restaurant again.

Visited Megumi recently and had a really enjoyable dining experience. The space feels refined and calm, with a warm, premium vibe that makes you want to slow down and enjoy the meal. Service was attentive without being intrusive and everything arrived on time and was explained well.

The food truly stood out. The salmon truffle cream cheese was smooth, rich and beautifully balanced, with the truffle adding depth without overpowering the dish. The chargrilled chicken was juicy and nicely smoked, cooked just right.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Some restaurants get the ambiance right.
Some focus entirely on the food.
And then there are places like Megumi that manage to do both beautifully.

From the moment we walked in, the space felt warm, elegant, and calming without trying too hard. The kind of restaurant where you instantly know you’re going to enjoy spending time — whether it’s for a quiet dinner, a catch-up with friends, or simply a slow evening over good food.

The meal began with complimentary sweet potato chips served alongside a jalapeño dip and chilli oil, and honestly, this small opening already set the tone for the evening. Crisp, addictive, and paired with dips that added both heat and freshness — it was one of those thoughtful touches that immediately makes you feel taken care of.

We then moved on to the Daikon Cake, which was beautifully executed with a lovely balance of texture and flavour. Comforting, delicate, and packed with umami, it was the kind of dish that quietly impresses you.

The Spicy Corn Curd was another standout for me. Creamy, flavourful, and carrying just the right amount of spice, it struck that perfect balance between indulgent and light. Definitely one of those dishes I’d happily reorder.

But the real star of the meal was the Edamame and Truffle Fried Rice. Fragrant, comforting, and deeply satisfying, this dish had everything working in its favour. The truffle flavour was present without overpowering the dish, while the edamame added texture and freshness. Easily one of the best things we ate that evening.

We also tried the Smoked Cottage Cheese Robata, which brought in beautiful smoky flavours while still letting the softness of the cottage cheese shine through. Rich, well-balanced, and very satisfying.

To end the meal, we had the Almond Coffee Delicai, which was smooth, indulgent, and the perfect finish to the evening. The coffee and almond combination worked beautifully together without feeling too heavy.

Final thoughts:
Megumi delivers exactly what you hope for from a good Asian dining experience — thoughtful food, balanced flavours, warm hospitality, and an ambiance that makes you want to stay longer. Every dish felt carefully crafted, and the overall meal struck that lovely balance between comfort and elegance.

A beautiful dining experience in Santacruz that I’d happily go back to. ✨

featured_reviews.name: Vipul G
featured_reviews.review_text:
Wok express is spreading its wings slowly but firmly across the city.. Most of them are like takeaway joints .. I happened to visit their bkc outlet on Sunday eve, my first experience at wok express, n it was good.. Wok express do serve oriental food at very reasonable rates.. The bkc outlet has 3 tables n few chairs to sit.. It's a very clean hygienic place.. I started here with zesty lemon n coriander soup.. This healthy n delicious soup had refreshing combination of lemon, coriander n veggies in it with a thick consistency .. We tried crispy tempura roll sushi n they were scrumptious.. Carrot, Onion, Tempura flour and Sesame oil rolled in sweet and sour rice are served along with soya sauce.. It was too good n one of the best sushi I have ever had.. Had kung pao potatoes n it was also very good .. Baby potatoes, cooked in Chinese sauce, are served along with roasted peanuts on it.. It was delectable n quite filling one.. We also tried chilli Paneer bao n I found it ok.. Chopped pieces of succulent Paneer are marinated well in spicy chilli basil sauce n are served in super soft fluffy bao.. I found it too much saucy to my liking.. Wok express is known for its wok n they here do serve some really amazing wok our here.. One can directly order for chef recommended wok box which I guess will be great to do.. One can also customise n choose between rice n noodles, sauces, veggies n condiments n prepare wok according to their liking if you are particular about what u eat.. Also there are sizes to choose from n along with combo deals with drinks it's very reasonable.. I had Bangkok ramen noodles n it was too good.. This wok box had ramen noodles along with veggies n sauce were topped with burnt garlic.. It was hot, tasty n treat to my taste buds.. Food overall was good here n let me warn u if u don't like medium spicy or spicy food this place is not for you.. We also tried popcorn n peach iced bubble tea n I found both to be good in flavour but frankly Tapioca pearls in it were not that great n i will recommend to try bubble tea without tapioca pearls in it.. Will like the management to work on tapioca pearls n improve on it.. Service was good n staff were very helpful with their recommendations.. As food is prepared fresh expect 10/15 mins wait for ur order.. Overall it was decent experience out here n I'm surely trying their other woks served out here in future

My recommendations - Zesty lemon n coriander soup, crispy tempura roll sushi, kung pao potatoes, Bangkok ramen noodles

Good budget place to drink in kalina, love the butter garlic chicken! Must try.

They don't have tandoori items though, only chinese.

featured_reviews.name: Virgin Braganza
featured_reviews.review_text: Had dinner at this restaurant some days ago .Tried out chicken lollipop for appetizers and fried rice for main course. The taste of food was delicious. The quantity of food was good enough to eat. The ambience is lovely with comfortable seating. The service too was good.

featured_reviews.name: Sebastian Braganza
featured_reviews.review_text: As a respect for the 3 lovely woman in my life, I had taken my mom & my 2 sisters to Taco Cheeno on Womens Day for dinner as this restaurant is 5 mins walkable distance from my house. We ordered chicken lollipop, schezwan fried rice & thai hot pot rice with gravy. The service was very quick by the attendants.For service I can say they were too good. The Manager also was polite as he was Goan & we are goans too, so we had some good talks in konkani.The food quality & quantity was very good.

featured_reviews.name: Raivat Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best place to have Chinese appetizers nd main course.All the dishes here are pocket friendly

featured_reviews.name: Dipanker Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
My friend Kishore Shetty recommended this place. A very nice cosy place for bachelors.

Must visit.

featured_reviews.name: SageRaj Bariya
featured_reviews.review_text: this is not a family place at all, ambience is just guys night out place, food quality is not so great or let say not so cheap food at high price. server is always in hurry , just to take one order and run away to kitchen. on the way to toilet you will see kitchen and thts when you will make decision to get out. half way through our night we 6 guys decided to end it and bill came to 3960, not at all cheap, but food quality was not at all good. visit at your own risk.

featured_reviews.name: Leo Noronha
featured_reviews.review_text: Local bar joint close to home.. their food is good and staff is less so you'd have to keep following up for things. The ambiance is low key and crowd is also low key. The menu is cheaper compared to surrounding bars.

featured_reviews.name: Chetan Pandit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I love this place for the variety of food. That's why I visit this place frequently. They serve amazingly delicious food. My favorite is Apple Chicken and Chilly Garlic Noodles.

Edit after 4 years, interiors have significantly deteriorated. Food quality has gone south. Was disappointed to see many of the previous best seller items being taken down from the menu.
